propositions: BindingStore owns coupled identity transition rules (bind, confirm, unbind, reverse cleanup, numeric-ID moves) that must be extracted into a single cohesive BindingLifecycle policy owner with dedicated table-driven tests over valid, missing, corrupt, duplicate, and stale forward/reverse combinations.
bind_confirm must remain last-writer-wins on forward entry, popping exactly one differing old reverse key with no sweep, ambiguity detection, or abort behavior.
Stale reverse entries may be removed only in four existing permitted cases: bind_confirm rebind, unbind, re-key, and _retire; any other removal must abort.
Numeric-ID re-key logic must move issues instead of retiring them, triggered only when _current_key_by_id returns a different key than the current entry's jira_key.

note_absent_or_rekey coordination must remain on the public facade: it delegates re-key attempt to lifecycle owner, and on negative result falls through to note_absent (which remains facade-owned until S2 T2), preserving all caller-visible outcomes and signature.
Every valid bind/confirm/unbind transition must leave at most one forward and one matching reverse identity, achieved by targeted single-key pops rather than by ambiguity detection or refusal.
